about: The full three-minute film's transcript and scene descriptions, from its production plan (cut-plan.json and narration-plan.json). The narration is the captions' text word for word, which tests/test_build_site.py checks. scripts/build_site.py renders it into site/film/index.html.
title: The full film: transcript and scene descriptions | ta-amps
description: The three-minute Eranos film's transcript and scene descriptions, in six parts: spare tokens for good, the architecture, nouns and verbs in plain words, why it matters and Meta's models, use it for anything, and how the film itself was made.
heading: The full film: transcript and scene descriptions
lead: Three minutes in six parts. Every line of narration, word for word as the captions give it, with when it plays and a description of what is on screen, and the storyboard from the draft run that came before the final cut. The film plays on the home page.
audio_description: A separate audio-described cut is not available yet. Until then, this page is the film's text alternative.

acts.name: The use case: spare tokens for good
Nouns and verbs, in plain words
Why it matters, and Meta's models

lines.words: If your AI plan has tokens left over at the end of the month…
lines.picture: A month's AI plan meter; the unused part fills with token tiles that lift off.
lines.on_screen: This month's AI plan · used · left over

lines.words: …Eranos puts them to work for nonprofits. Spare tokens for good.
lines.picture: The tiles fly into the Eranos mark; the title card.
lines.on_screen: Eranos · Spare tokens for good. · Your unused AI capacity, doing real work for nonprofits.

lines.words: Nonprofits say what they need, in plain words. Public research comes back finished and cited. Work on their own files becomes a kit their own agent runs.
lines.picture: On the live Eranos website, a visitor clicks I work at a nonprofit, opens /nonprofits, submits a plain-language intake request, and scrolls the live /requests/REQ-INTAKE-07 status page as the request splits into cited public budget research and a local handwritten-statements agent kit.
lines.on_screen: eranos.ta-amps.workers.dev · /nonprofits · /requests/REQ-INTAKE-07

lines.words: Anyone can help: pick an open task, and hand it to your own AI agent.
lines.picture: The live /help page: connect your agent, copy a starting brief, the open tasks.
lines.on_screen: eranos.ta-amps.workers.dev/help

lines.words: Your agent claims the task. Only one agent works on it at a time, and every step gets a receipt.
lines.picture: Volunteer A's recorded terminal session in the local run: list tasks, claim the scope check, pass it, claim the build, with lease and claim receipts.
lines.on_screen: claimed · only volunteer-a can submit · claim receipt

lines.words: A different volunteer's agent reviews it. The builder can never approve its own kit.
lines.picture: Volunteer A tries to approve its own kit and is refused; volunteer B claims the review, re-runs the checks, approves and publishes.
lines.on_screen: refused · two-step rule · approved · published

lines.words: Now the nonprofit has a free, reviewed kit.
lines.picture: The published kit's page in the local catalog: what the agent drafts and what stays with a person, then the review receipts.
lines.on_screen: Agent drafts · Person only · Review receipts

lines.words: We built the nonprofit marketplace first, because AI has to help everyone, not just the tech world.
lines.picture: Eranos's live home page and its two doors, while the voice says why the nonprofit side comes first.
lines.on_screen: Built first: the nonprofit marketplace

lines.words: Now, the radically flexible architecture that runs it, and can be repurposed.
lines.picture: A section card; the bridge into the architecture is spoken over it.
lines.on_screen: Part 2 of 6 · The architecture · Radically flexible, and it can be repurposed

lines.words: It isn't a new kind of model. It's a new way to organize the work.
lines.picture: Motion graphics: a crossed-out model stack beside organized tiles; the verb card (claim, do, report); the noun card (its kinds, described, searchable, versioned, usable with permission, linked into whole systems).
lines.on_screen: Not a model architecture: a way to organize the work · verb = task · noun = thing

lines.words: Verbs are tasks: the smallest piece of work a worker can claim, do and report.
lines.on_screen: Not a model architecture: a way to organize the work · verb = task · noun = thing

lines.words: Nouns are everything a task uses or makes: described, searchable, usable with permission, and linkable into whole systems.
lines.on_screen: Not a model architecture: a way to organize the work · verb = task · noun = thing

lines.words: Say someone asks for a data-cleaning pipeline. It becomes one verb, and the agent holding it splits it up.
lines.picture: Illustration, not a measured run: a data-cleaning pipeline request becomes a verb, and the agent holding it splits it; workers claim the pieces; every input, output and trace drops in as a noun; a worker adds verbs; a final verb combines them into one searchable solution noun.
lines.on_screen: Request → one verb → smaller verbs on a queue → workers anywhere → nouns → combine → solution noun

lines.words: Workers anywhere claim the pieces, and every input, output and trace becomes a noun.
lines.on_screen: Request → one verb → smaller verbs on a queue → workers anywhere → nouns → combine → solution noun

lines.words: A final verb combines them into one solution: a searchable noun.
lines.on_screen: Request → one verb → smaller verbs on a queue → workers anywhere → nouns → combine → solution noun

lines.words: When someone else asks for the same pipeline, search finds it: no new work, and no new tokens.
lines.picture: Illustration, not a measured run: a second team asks for the same pipeline; search finds the stored solution noun; no new work and no new tokens.
lines.on_screen: The same request · search · found · 0 new model tokens

lines.words: Tessera keeps the queue and the nouns. Herma, the shim, brings the right ones to any agent.
lines.picture: Illustration of the two pieces of infrastructure.
lines.on_screen: Tessera keeps the queue and the nouns · Herma, the shim, brings the right nouns to any agent

lines.words: AI is smart. The way we use it is frustratingly dumb.
lines.picture: A section card; the deck's cover line is spoken over it.
lines.on_screen: Part 4 of 6 · Why it matters · AI is smart. The way we use it is frustratingly dumb.

lines.words: It doesn't know what's new, it rewrites what exists, and it needs babysitting.
lines.picture: Motion graphics: three problems plus one, each mapped to its fix: feeds; search and retrieval; verbs on a shared queue; tuning, measured on tests we wrote.
lines.on_screen: It doesn't know what's new · rewrites what exists · needs babysitting · training alone doesn't fix it

lines.words: Say you need a memory system, and hundreds appear on GitHub in two days. Workers gather them and their benchmarks as nouns, and your agent just asks which fits.
lines.picture: Illustration (the repo and paper feeds are planned, not running): hundreds of new memory systems; workers gather them and comparable benchmarks as nouns; the agent asks each week. Then the real precedent: the deterministic scan of the hackathon's public repos.
lines.on_screen: ILLUSTRATION · a memory system for your agents · comparison noun · weekly question · real: 705 of 739 repos scanned

lines.words: Tuning made Meta's models measurably better on tests we wrote: Llama 3.2 from 12 to 51 percent, and Muse Glimmer from 93 to 99.
lines.picture: The deck's measured tuning results on tests we wrote, named aloud and on screen, and Muse Code and nanoMuse as workers.
lines.on_screen: Meta's models, measurably better · Llama 3.2 1B 12.0% → 50.7% · 3B 52.0% → 72.7% · Muse Glimmer 30B 93.3% → 99.3%

lines.words: Workers run on Meta's models too, like Meta's Muse Code on Muse Spark.
lines.on_screen: Meta's models, measurably better · Llama 3.2 1B 12.0% → 50.7% · 3B 52.0% → 72.7% · Muse Glimmer 30B 93.3% → 99.3%

lines.words: The same nouns and verbs fit almost any project.
lines.picture: Agora's live use-cases page.
lines.on_screen: Grant writing · Literature reviews · Checked data pipelines

lines.words: Connect any agent with Agora's instructions.
lines.picture: Agora's live Agent compatible banner and its Copy instructions button; Tessera's live tool count, read from its public agent pages.
lines.on_screen: Copy instructions · 37 tools

lines.words: Or make your own seed pack, and submit it.
lines.picture: The roll-your-own deck's make-a-seed-pack slide, then the pull-back into the board.
lines.on_screen: Make a seed pack

lines.words: This entire video was made from nouns and verbs, claimed and finished by workers on Tessera, with a receipt for every step.
lines.picture: Pull back from the picture into a 'this video' noun tile; the board of this video's verbs and receipts, read from the local production Tessera store.
lines.on_screen: THIS VIDEO · NOUNS AND VERBS

lines.words: Start at Agora, and point your agent at Eranos.
lines.picture: Agora's home and Eranos, with both addresses.
lines.on_screen: Start at Agora · Point your agent at Eranos

note: Narration is an AI voice (Kokoro, af_heart). Every example in the film uses made-up data, and every number comes from a measured, task we wrote.
